newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot gas prices driven lower by mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot gas prices driven lower by mild weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices for the last day of December continued to falter Monday, pressured by forecasts for well above-normal temperatures throughout most of the U.S. this week, sources said.
December Gulf Coast prices fell another 40 cents to the $2.70-2.80 per mmBtu range, down about $1.20 from week-ago levels.

Early January swing prices were talked in the $2.80-2.98 range at the Henry Hub, as the NYMEX February futures contract traded to a low of $2.63. Most traders agreed January spot business was on the backburner until next year.
At the New York city-gate, prices were talked in the $3.40-3.50 range for the last day of December, steady to down slightly from Friday's levels.
Temperatures in the Mid-Atlantic states are expected to return to near-normal Tuesday and Wednesday but then climb to above-normal levels through early next week.
Midcontinent prices continued to erode in very thin trade, with most price discussion in the $2.70-2.75 range, down more than 15 cents from Friday.
"No one is even talking about January," one Midcontinent source said, noting most are equipped to meet demand over the first few days of the new year due to the mild weather moving into the region.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices were talked in the $2.60-2.80 range, down from Friday's wider range of $2.60-3.25.
Early discussion of January Permian business was in the low-$3 area.
